subject: Falcon AI - elevated timeouts & client-side retry feedback (incident wrap)
body:
From: Elena Mendez <emendez@falcon.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@falcon.ai
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in timeouts / 429s this morning - need quick sync

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a large number of timeouts and 429 responses against our production routes at ~08:45 PDT this morning. Latency jumped from our usual p50~70ms to sustained >1s and a flurry of client retries made the errors worse. Our monitoring shows retries from several microservices that then trigger downstream throttling.

Can someone on your side confirm whether there was any deployment, scaling event, or quota change around that time? This is impacting customer transactions (payments flow) and legal is starting to get pinged. Any immediate mitigation steps you can take would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Mendez
Head of Ops, Falcon AI

-----
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mendez <emendez@falcon.ai>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in timeouts / 429s this morning - need quick sync

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the outage. Looping in Dev and Sean for immediate triage.

Quick status from my side: no scheduled platform deploy at 08:45; we did have an automated scale event on the dedicated pool in us-west-2 that started at 08:40 due to a sudden concurrency bump, but the autoscaler reported several failed attempts to attach workers (AWS API rate errors). That could explain transient capacity gaps and a retry storm.

Dev / Sean: please pull logs for the failed attach attempts and check our worker provisioning throttles. Also confirm whether the fallback model variant routing was triggered.

I will keep Falcon posted.

—Rishi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

-----
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in timeouts / 429s this morning - need quick sync

Logging notes (initial triage):
- Autoscaler invoked to add 6 worker nodes at 08:40 due to sustained queue growth.
- Control plane saw a burst of AWS "RequestLimitExceeded" (EC2) between 08:41–08:46; several provisioning calls retried and eventually succeeded at ~08:59.
- During 08:45–09:05 window we observed elevated 429s from the token bucket limiter on the serving runtime (component: request-rate-limiter) and per-model token cache thrashing leading to timeouts.
- Prefix cache hit rate dropped by ~27% due to many short-lived sessions (client retry loops).

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:12:
- Temporarily raised runtime limiter from 1200 RPS -> 1800 RPS for Falcon routing rule (manual override).
- Enabled emergency KV cache retention policy to reduce cache churn for the next hour.
- Throttled inbound retries via a short-lived global retry-backoff response header (Retry-After: 2s) returned by the gateway.

I attached the compressed control plane log snippets (falcon_incident_log_0504.zip) and a short timeline. Next: we should follow up with permanent alerting and a runbook.

—Dev
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mendez <emendez@falcon.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in timeouts / 429s this morning - need quick sync

Elena — thanks for your patience. I spoke with our CS lead; we confirmed the payment flow errors were concentrated in a specific Falcon tenant. We pushed the temporary limiter increase and cache fix; Falcon reports improvements around 09:20 and saw a gradual recovery by 10:05.

Customer communication: I recommended the Falcon team implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter (we gave them a snippet) and asked them to pause aggressive cron-based reconciliation jobs they said were active during the window.

Marissa Cole
Senior AM, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

-----
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 18:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in timeouts / 429s this morning - need quick sync

Follow-ups from ops:
- Root cause (candidate): provisioning throttles + insufficient emergency autoscale headroom for dedicated pool; combined with client retry amplification.
- Alerts that did fire were noisy and not specific: the autoscaler emitted generic failure alerts but there was no single consolidated SLO breach alert for Falcon's critical payment route. No runbook link was surfaced in the alert.
- Suggested short-term actions: add a dedicated SLO alert for Falcon payment route (p99 latency > 700ms sustained 5m OR error rate > 2% for 5m).
- Longer-term: increase pre-warmed capacity for high-tier tenants, add exponential backoff enforcement guidance, and add control-plane rate-limit escalation runbook.

I'm opening INF-4672 to track (attached to related_links).

—Sean
Director, Site Reliability Engineering

-----
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mendez <emendez@falcon.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Falcon 0504 incident — postmortem summary & actions (owner assignments)

Team / Elena — thanks everyone for the quick responses. Below is the postmortem summary and concrete action items; attached is a short slide deck for execs and a CSV with owners/timelines.

Summary:
- Symptom: elevated p99 latency and 5xx/429 spike for Falcon tenant payment routes between 08:40–09:05 PDT on 2026-05-04, caused by control-plane provisioning rate limits which delayed worker attachment and created capacity gaps. Amplified by aggressive client retries and prefix KV cache churn.
- Impact: Falcon reported customer-facing payment failures and increased support load; duration ~25m; revenue-impacting transactions affected for a subset of tenants.

Action items (owner — ETA):
1) Alerts & runbooks — Sean (2 business days): create a targeted SLO alert for tenant payment routes, consolidate related autoscaler/control-plane alerts into a single incident alert that surfaces the runbook link.
2) Pre-warm capacity policy — Evelyn (1 week): define pre-warm headroom rules for tiered tenants and implement pre-provisioning when sustained concurrency growth detected.
3) Control-plane rate limits — Dev (3 business days): add smarter retry/backoff for provisioning API calls, exponential backoff with capped retries, and fallback to alternative AZs.
4) SDK guidance & enforcement — Marissa (3 business days): publish SDK best-practices for backoff/jitter and provide a one-page integration checklist to Falcon.
5) SLO tuning & traffic shaping — Rishi (2 business days): adjust temporary p99 thresholds and add a traffic-shaping policy for very high short-lived bursts that could otherwise starve long sessions.
6) Post-incident customer package — Marissa (2 business days): send Falcon the postmortem slide deck + credits as agreed by sales/legal.

Ownership notes: I will coordinate the exec-facing summary and follow up with Falcon's CRO tomorrow. Please update INF-4672 with progress and mark items done as you close them. We will schedule a 30-minute retrospective with Falcon ops on Friday.

Attachments: postmortem-slides-0505.pdf, slo_action_items.csv (owners/ETA)

Thanks — let’s treat the runbook/comms work as highest priority to avoid similar escalations.

—Rishi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
